cards.title: StudyFetch Calendar 2.0 - the calendar decides what to study
cards.move: Open on the pain, not the product: the first beat is the student deciding what to study tonight, and the calendar answers it - exam, topics, mastery - so the UI enters as the answer to a question the viewer already has.
cards.why: StudyAI's hook is the same pain (page in, no idea where to start). Borrowing the problem-first order means the device beat proves something instead of introducing a screen.

cards.title: Gemini study notebooks - curiosity to comprehension
cards.move: Sell the transformation in one line and make free/available part of the promise, not a footnote: the film never lists features, it names the before and after state and closes on the access condition (free, every language).
cards.why: Our CTA already ends on 'جاهز أن تبدأ؟ مجانًا'; this is the register to keep - one transformation, then access, nothing invented about scale or ratings.

cards.title: Shape morphing through UI states - prompt-motion
cards.move: One element, never cut: size, radius and colour morph while the content swaps with a short blur, every value a closed-form spring summed per event, all of it a pure function of seek(t); drags are direct manipulation and the loop closes on frame 0.
cards.why: This is exactly how a UI beat should behave in our engine: no transitions, no state, one spring per change, so --concurrency=75% cannot change the picture.
